source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους, εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus all the words these, he said to the disciples of him:

en.L: And it happened, when Jesus had finished all these words, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,
en.B: When Jesus had finished all these words, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,
en.R: Jesus finished teaching all these things. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers,

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished all these words: the formula that closes the last of the five long speeches
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech this way (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1). Only here does he add "all", closing the speech of chapters 24-25 and perhaps the whole of Jesus's teaching before the passion.

decisions.choice: When Jesus had finished all these words
alternatives: When Jesus had finished saying all these things
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wording of the same formula at 7:28.

source.text: Οἴδατε ὅτι μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας τὸ πάσχα γίνεται, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς τὸ σταυρωθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of the Man is handed over for the to be crucified.

en.L: "You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."
en.B: "As you know, the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified."
en.R: "You know that the Passover festival is two days from now. At that time the Son of Man will be handed over to be killed on a cross."

decisions.choice: the Passover: the yearly feast remembering Israel's rescue from Egypt
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed on the fourteenth of the month Nisan and eaten that night (Exodus 12:1-14). The seven days of Unleavened Bread followed, and pilgrims crowded into Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: is handed over: given up to his enemies, by Judas and in God's plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. It is used of Judas (10:4; 26:15) and in Jesus's earlier predictions of his death (17:22; 20:18-19).

decisions.choice: is handed over: the present tense for what is certain to happen soon
alternatives: is being handed over at this moment
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the coming event as already under way.

decisions.choice: will be handed over
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the future, since the event is two days away.

decisions.choice: to be killed on a cross; at that time
decisions.reason: Readable explains crucifixion and links the two events, as the "and" of the Greek implies.

source.text: Τότε συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τοῦ λεγομένου Καϊάφα, καὶ συνεβουλεύσαντο ἵνα τὸν Ἰησοῦν δόλῳ κρατήσωσιν καὶ ἀποκτείνωσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Then were gathered the chief priests and the elders of the people in the courtyard of the high priest, the one called Caiaphas, \v 4 and they plotted together that the Jesus by deceit they might seize and kill;

en.L: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas, \v 4 and they plotted together to seize Jesus by deceit and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people met in the courtyard of the high priest, a man named Caiaphas. \v 4 There they made plans to arrest Jesus by some trick and put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death.
en.R: At that time the leading priests and the older leaders of the people met at the home of the high priest. His name was Caiaphas. \v 4 They made a plan to arrest Jesus secretly and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Caiaphas: high priest from about AD 18 to 36
decisions.reason: Joseph Caiaphas held the office longer than any other high priest under Roman rule. John 18:13 says he was the son-in-law of Annas, an earlier high priest.

decisions.choice: courtyard: the open court of the high priest's residence, or the residence itself
decisions.reason: The word means an enclosed courtyard and can stand for the whole palace around it. The same place appears in 26:58 and 26:69.

decisions.choice: by deceit: by stealth, away from the crowds
decisions.reason: They want to take him quietly, by some trick, for fear of the people (26:5).

decisions.choice: leading priests; older leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says who these groups were, as in 2:4.

source.text: ἔλεγον δέ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, ἵνα μὴ θόρυβος γένηται ἐν τῷ λαῷ.

records.literal_gloss: They were saying but, Not at the feast, so that not an uproar happens among the people.

en.L: But they were saying, "Not during the feast, so that there may not be an uproar among the people."
en.B: But they kept saying, "Not at the festival. We do not want the people to riot."
en.R: But they said, "We must not do it during the festival. The people might start a riot."

decisions.choice: an uproar among the people: the crowds of pilgrims, many of whom welcomed Jesus
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was crowded at Passover, and the crowds had hailed Jesus (21:8-11). The leaders had already held back for fear of them (21:46).

decisions.choice: not during the feast: not in the festival days
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the days of the feast or the crowd gathered for it. Either way they want to avoid a public arrest; in the end Judas's offer lets them act at once.

decisions.choice: We do not want (B); The people might (R)
alternatives: so that there may not be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the purpose clause into a plain statement of the leaders' fear.

source.text: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ, προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου βαρυτίμου καὶ κατέχεεν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus being in Bethany in house of Simon the leper, \v 7 came to him a woman having an alabaster flask of ointment very costly and poured [it] on the head of him reclining.

en.L: Now while Jesus was in Bethany, in [the] house of Simon the leper, \v 7 a woman came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} having an alabaster jar of very costly ointment, and she poured [it] on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table].
en.B: While Jesus was at Bethany in the home of Simon, a man who had suffered from a skin disease, \v 7 a woman came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfumed oil. As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat at the table, she poured it over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.R: Jesus was in the town of Bethany. He was at the house of a man named Simon, who had once had a bad skin disease. \v 7 While Jesus was eating there, a woman came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. She had a beautiful stone jar full of perfume that cost a great deal of money. She poured the perfume on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

decisions.choice: Simon the leper: known by a skin disease he had once had, probably healed
alternatives: a man still unclean with the disease
decisions.reason: A man still unclean could not have received guests at his table (Leviticus 13:45-46). The name may recall a past illness, perhaps one Jesus healed (8:2-3).

decisions.choice: an alabaster jar of very costly ointment: a sealed stone jar of perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a soft, translucent stone used for jars of perfume. Mark 14:3 says she broke the jar to pour it; Mark 14:5 values it at more than three hundred denarii, about a year's wages.

decisions.choice: poured it on his head: an act of honor, recalling the anointing of kings
decisions.reason: Oil was poured on a guest's head as an honor (Psalm 23:5), and kings were anointed on the head (1 Samuel 10:1). Jesus himself gives the act its meaning in 26:12.

decisions.choice: a man who had suffered from a skin disease (B); who had once had a bad skin disease (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:2, Balanced and Readable describe the disease. Saying it was in the past follows meaning decision m1 and is not certain.

source.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἠγανάκτησαν λέγοντες· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη;

records.literal_gloss: Having seen but the disciples were indignant saying, For what the waste this?

en.L: But when the disciples saw [it], they were indignant, saying, "Why this waste?
en.B: Seeing this, the disciples were indignant. They said, "What is the point of such waste?
en.R: When the followers saw this, they were upset. They said, "Why waste all that perfume?

decisions.choice: the disciples: Matthew speaks of the group
decisions.reason: John 12:4-6 names Judas as the one who complained. Matthew says the disciples as a whole objected.

decisions.choice: waste: loss, something thrown away
decisions.reason: The word means ruin or loss; here money poured out for nothing, as they see it.

source.text: ἐδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο πραθῆναι πολλοῦ καὶ δοθῆναι πτωχοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Could for this to be sold for much and to be given to poor.

en.L: For this could have been sold for much and given to [the] poor."
en.B: It could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor."
en.R: It could have been sold for a lot of money. Then the money could have been given to poor people."

decisions.choice: given to the poor: gifts to the poor were expected, especially at Passover
alternatives: a new idea of the disciples
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:11) and was linked with the feast (John 13:29).

decisions.choice: the money
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the money, not the perfume, would be given.

source.text: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί;

records.literal_gloss: Having known but the Jesus said to them, Why troubles you cause to the woman?

en.L: But Jesus, knowing [this], said to them, "Why do you cause the woman trouble?
en.B: Jesus was aware of this and said to them, "Why make trouble for this woman?
en.R: Jesus knew what they were saying. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you upsetting this woman?

decisions.choice: knowing this: Jesus became aware of their complaint
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say how he knew; they may have spoken openly.

decisions.choice: cause trouble: bother, distress
decisions.reason: The phrase means to give someone grief or annoyance, here by criticizing her.

source.text: ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν ἠργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ·

records.literal_gloss: A work for good she worked for me;

en.L: For she has done a beautiful work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: What she has done for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is a beautiful thing.
en.R: She has done a good and lovely thing for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: beautiful: good and fitting
alternatives: good only in the moral sense
decisions.reason: The word joins what is good with what is fine and fitting. Her act was right for the moment.

decisions.choice: good and lovely
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the word.

source.text: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·

records.literal_gloss: Always for the poor you have with yourselves, me but not always you have;

en.L: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The poor will always be among you, but I will not always be with you.
en.R: There will always be poor people among you. But I will not always be here with you.

decisions.choice: you always have the poor with you: Deuteronomy 15:11
decisions.reason: The law says the poor will never cease from the land, and so God's people must open their hand to them. Jesus does not set aside that duty.

decisions.choice: not always have me: Jesus points to his coming death
alternatives: he is leaving on a journey
decisions.reason: The time with him is short (26:2, 12), so honoring him now is fitting.

decisions.choice: I will not always be with you
alternatives: you do not always have me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Jesus the subject, which is more natural English.

source.text: βαλοῦσα γὰρ αὕτη τὸ μύρον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματός μου πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ἐποίησεν.

records.literal_gloss: Having poured for this [woman] the ointment this on the body of me, for the to prepare for burial me she did [it].

en.L: For in pouring this ointment on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, she did [it] to prepare {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for burial.
en.B: By pouring this perfume over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, she has made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ready to be buried.
en.R: She put this perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body to get {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ready to be buried.

decisions.choice: to prepare me for burial: bodies were anointed with oil and spices for burial
decisions.reason: Jews anointed the dead before burial (Mark 16:1; John 19:39-40). Jesus says this anointing comes before his death.

decisions.choice: she did it for my burial: Jesus gives the act its meaning
alternatives: she knew he was about to die
decisions.reason: The words may mean that she intended it so, or that Jesus declares what her act means. The text does not say how much she understood.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ, λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, wherever is proclaimed the gospel this in whole the world, will be spoken also what did this [woman] for a memorial of her.

en.L: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what this [woman] has done will also be spoken of in memory of her."
en.B: Truly I tell you, in every place in the whole world where this gospel is proclaimed, people will also tell what she has done, so that she is remembered."
en.R: I tell you the truth. This good news will be told all over the world. And wherever it is told, people will also tell what this woman did. They will remember her."

decisions.choice: this gospel: the good news of the kingdom, now including Jesus's death
decisions.reason: "Gospel" means good news (4:23; 24:14). "This" ties it to the death for which she has anointed him.

decisions.choice: the whole world: all nations and peoples
decisions.reason: As in 24:14 and 28:19, the good news is to go to every nation.

decisions.choice: in memory of her: so that she will be remembered
decisions.reason: The word can mean a reminder before God (Acts 10:4). Here the telling of her act keeps her memory alive among people.

decisions.choice: told
decisions.reason: Readable uses a simpler word for public announcing.

source.text: Τότε πορευθεὶς εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριώτης, πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς εἶπεν· Τί θέλετέ μοι δοῦναι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Then having gone one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, to the chief priests \v 15 said, What are you willing to me to give, and I to you will hand over him?

en.L: Then one of the Twelve, the [one] called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests \v 15 [and] said, "What are you willing to give me? And I will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to you."
en.B: Then one of the Twelve, the man called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests \v 15 and asked, "How much will you pay me to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to you?"
en.R: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve followers, went to the leading priests. \v 15 He asked them, "What will you pay me if I hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to you?"

decisions.choice: then: Judas acts right after the anointing
decisions.reason: Matthew sets Judas's bargain beside the woman's costly gift and Jesus's talk of burial.

decisions.choice: hand him over: betray him to his enemies
alternatives: give him up in a lawful way
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. Used of Judas it means betrayal (10:4).

decisions.choice: what will you give me, and I will hand him over: a bargain
decisions.reason: The "and" links the price and the deed: give me something and I will do it.

decisions.choice: How much will you pay me (B); What will you pay me (R)
alternatives: What are you willing to give me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the bargain plainly.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια.

records.literal_gloss: They and weighed out to him thirty silver pieces.

en.L: And they weighed out to him thirty pieces of silver.
en.B: They paid him thirty silver coins.
en.R: So they paid him thirty silver coins.

decisions.choice: weighed out: paid him the money
decisions.reason: The verb means to set or to weigh out, and it is the word for weighing wages in Zechariah 11:12. Mark 14:11 says they promised to give him money, and some take Matthew's word in that sense.

decisions.choice: thirty pieces of silver: Zechariah 11:12
decisions.reason: In Zechariah the shepherd's wages are thirty pieces of silver, a sum he calls a fine price, in scorn. Matthew returns to the passage in 27:9-10. Thirty shekels was also the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32).

decisions.choice: thirty pieces of silver: probably silver shekels, worth about four months' wages
decisions.reason: The coin is not named. If they were shekels, each worth about four denarii, the sum was about one hundred twenty days' wages for a laborer.

decisions.choice: thirty silver coins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name coins. Because the coin is not named, no modern equivalent is given; meaning decision m3 gives the likely value. Literal keeps the familiar wording.

source.text: καὶ ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And from then he was seeking opportunity that him he might hand over.

en.L: And from then on he was seeking an opportunity to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: After that, Judas kept looking for the right moment to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.R: From then on, Judas waited for a good time to hand Jesus over to them.

decisions.choice: opportunity: a fitting time, away from the crowds
decisions.reason: The leaders wanted to avoid an uproar (26:5). Judas looks for a time when Jesus is alone with his disciples.

decisions.choice: Judas (B, R); Jesus; to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Judas, and Readable also names Jesus, to make clear who is meant.
